title: Earth's Features
description: Earth has land features like mountains, valleys, and plains. Water covers most of Earth as oceans, lakes, and rivers. Earth has many natural resources.

exercises.question: What covers most of Earth's surface?
exercises.exp: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water — mostly the oceans!

exercises.question: Which is the LARGEST body of water?
exercises.exp: Oceans are the largest bodies of water. Earth has five oceans!

exercises.question: What is a MOUNTAIN?
choices: a very tall area of land rising sharply from the ground
exercises.exp: Mountains are very tall, steep landforms. The Rocky Mountains are in Canada!

exercises.question: What is a VALLEY?
choices: a low area of land between hills or mountains
a flat area near the ocean
exercises.exp: Valleys are low areas between hills or mountains — often a river flows through them.

exercises.question: Which is a natural resource from the EARTH?
exercises.exp: Fresh water is a natural resource — it comes from the Earth and is essential for life.

exercises.question: What is SOIL made of?
choices: tiny bits of rock, minerals, and decayed plants and animals
exercises.exp: Soil is a mix of tiny rock pieces, minerals, and decomposed organic matter — perfect for growing plants!

exercises.question: Which body of water is SURROUNDED by land on all sides?
exercises.exp: Lakes are completely surrounded by land. Canada has more lakes than any other country!

exercises.question: A river always flows ___.
choices: downward from higher to lower land
exercises.exp: Rivers flow downhill due to gravity — from mountains and hills down to lakes, seas, or oceans.

exercises.question: Which is a RENEWABLE natural resource?
exercises.exp: Sunlight is renewable — the sun keeps shining every day! Coal and oil take millions of years to form.

exercises.question: What is a PLAIN?
choices: a large flat area of land
exercises.exp: Plains are large, flat areas of land — they are great for farming! The prairies in Canada are plains.

exercises.question: What is a PENINSULA?
choices: a piece of land almost surrounded by water
exercises.exp: A peninsula sticks out into the water and is connected to the mainland on one side.

exercises.question: Why is FRESH WATER important for humans?
choices: we use it for drinking, cooking, and growing food
we use it to make cars
we use it to make electricity only
we use it as building material
exercises.exp: Fresh water is essential for drinking, cooking, bathing, and growing the food we eat.

exercises.question: What is a HILL?
choices: a flat area near the ocean
a raised area of land that is smaller and less steep than a mountain
exercises.exp: Hills are raised landforms — gentler and smaller than mountains. They are common across Canada!

exercises.question: What is a DELTA?
choices: a triangle-shaped area of land formed where a river meets the sea
exercises.exp: A delta forms when a river slows down at its mouth and deposits sediment — creating a fan-shaped landform.

exercises.question: Which of the following is a NON-RENEWABLE resource?
exercises.exp: Coal is non-renewable — it takes millions of years to form and cannot be replaced quickly once used up.

exercises.question: Canada has more LAKES than any other country. Why are lakes important?
choices: they are only used for swimming
they provide fresh water, habitat for wildlife, and support communities
exercises.exp: Lakes supply fresh drinking water, support ecosystems, allow fishing, and are used for recreation and transportation.

exercises.question: What is an ISLAND?
choices: a peninsula connected to the mainland
a piece of land completely surrounded by water
a flat plain near the ocean
exercises.exp: An island is land surrounded by water on all sides. Canada has more islands than any other country, including Baffin Island!

exercises.question: What is the OCEAN FLOOR like?
choices: it has mountains, valleys, and plains just like land
it is made entirely of sand
it is covered only by ice
exercises.exp: The ocean floor has its own mountains (mid-ocean ridges), deep trenches, plains, and volcanoes — just as varied as land!

exercises.question: TOPSOIL is the dark, top layer of soil. Why is it important?
choices: it is used to make roads
it is rich in nutrients and supports plant growth
it is used for drinking water
it reflects sunlight away from Earth
exercises.exp: Topsoil is packed with nutrients, minerals, and organisms. Most plants grow their roots in this fertile top layer.

exercises.question: What is a WETLAND?
choices: an area of land that is flooded with water for all or part of the year
exercises.exp: Wetlands (marshes, swamps, bogs) are important habitats — they filter water, prevent flooding, and support huge biodiversity.

exercises.question: What is a GLACIER?
choices: a very large, slow-moving mass of ice
exercises.exp: Glaciers are massive rivers of ice that move very slowly, carving valleys and shaping the land as they go.

exercises.question: The CANADIAN SHIELD is a large rocky region of Canada. What kind of land feature is it?
choices: a vast area of ancient exposed bedrock
exercises.exp: The Canadian Shield is one of the world's oldest rock formations — a huge region of ancient, hard bedrock across central Canada.

exercises.question: What is a TRIBUTARY?
choices: a smaller river or stream that flows into a larger river
exercises.exp: Tributaries are smaller streams that join a main river — like branches on a tree flowing into the trunk!

exercises.question: What is a CLIFF?
choices: a gentle slope leading to water
a very steep or vertical face of rock or earth
exercises.exp: Cliffs are steep, near-vertical rock faces — formed by erosion from waves, rivers, or glaciers over time.

exercises.question: Which layer of soil contains the MOST rock particles and few nutrients?
exercises.exp: Subsoil sits below topsoil — it has more rock particles, less organic matter, and fewer nutrients than topsoil.

exercises.question: What are SAND DUNES?
choices: hills made of sand shaped by wind
exercises.exp: Sand dunes are hills of sand formed by wind blowing sand into piles — found in deserts and along beaches!

exercises.question: The PRAIRIES of Canada are an example of which landform?
exercises.exp: The Canadian Prairies (Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta) are vast flat plains — excellent for growing wheat and other crops!

exercises.question: What is a CANYON?
choices: a wide, shallow valley with gentle slopes
a deep, narrow valley with steep sides carved by a river
a flat plain near the ocean
a small lake in the mountains
exercises.exp: Canyons are deep valleys with nearly vertical walls — carved by rivers over millions of years, like the Grand Canyon!

exercises.question: How do people use NATURAL RESOURCES from the Earth?
choices: for food, building, energy, and making products we need
exercises.exp: We use resources from Earth for almost everything — trees for wood, soil for farming, water for drinking, minerals for technology.

exercises.question: What is a FJORD?
choices: a long, deep, narrow inlet of the sea between steep cliffs — often formed by glaciers
exercises.exp: Fjords are dramatic coastal inlets carved by ancient glaciers. Canada (especially British Columbia) has many beautiful fjords!

exercises.question: Why is SOIL important for life on Earth?
choices: soil is only useful for building houses
soil provides nutrients and anchorage for plants, which in turn feed animals and humans
soil reflects heat from the sun
exercises.exp: Healthy soil grows the plants that feed all life. Without soil, we couldn't grow food — it is one of our most precious resources!

exercises.question: What is BEDROCK?
choices: the solid layer of rock underneath all the soil and subsoil layers
the layer of ice at the north pole
exercises.exp: Bedrock is the hard, solid rock layer deep under all the soil layers — the foundation everything else sits on!

exercises.question: Earth's outer rocky layer is called the ___.
exercises.exp: Earth's crust is the thin outer rocky layer we live on. Under the oceans it is only 5-10 km thick; under continents up to 70 km!

exercises.question: The hot, semi-liquid layer below Earth's crust is called the ___.
exercises.exp: The mantle is the thick layer between the crust and core. It is mostly solid rock but flows very slowly over millions of years.

exercises.question: Earth's INNER CORE is made mainly of ___.
exercises.exp: Earth's inner core is solid iron and nickel — under enormous pressure. It is incredibly hot (about 5000°C) but solid due to pressure!

exercises.question: What is a PENINSULA?
choices: an island completely surrounded by water
a piece of land with water on three sides, connected to the mainland on one side
a mountain range in the sea
a very flat area of land
exercises.exp: A peninsula is land jutting out into water on three sides. Florida and the Italian 'boot' are famous peninsulas!

exercises.question: Which landform is LOWEST and flat, often good for farming?
exercises.exp: Plains are large flat or gently rolling areas — usually low-lying. Their fertile soils and flat terrain make them perfect for farming!

exercises.question: A PLATEAU is different from a plain because ___.
choices: a plateau is higher than the surrounding land — like a flat-topped mountain
plateaus have water on all sides
exercises.exp: A plateau is a flat elevated area — high ground with a flat top. The Tibetan Plateau is the world's highest and largest!

exercises.question: What is a DELTA?
choices: a fan-shaped landform formed where a river drops sediment as it enters a larger body of water
a mountain formed by volcanic activity
a canyon carved by a glacier
exercises.exp: Deltas form where rivers slow down at their mouths — dropping sediment that builds up into fertile fan-shaped land. The Nile Delta is famous!

exercises.question: A GLACIER is ___.
choices: a large, slow-moving mass of ice formed from compacted snow over many years
exercises.exp: Glaciers are rivers of ice! They form over thousands of years and slowly carve valleys and landscapes as they move.

exercises.question: What type of rock is formed when magma cools and hardens?
exercises.exp: Igneous rocks form when magma (underground) or lava (on the surface) cools and solidifies. Granite and basalt are igneous rocks!

exercises.question: SEDIMENTARY rocks are formed by ___.
choices: layers of sediment being compressed and cemented over time
exercises.exp: Sedimentary rocks form when layers of sand, mud, and fossils are compressed over millions of years. Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary!

exercises.question: What does EROSION do to the landscape?
choices: it wears away and carries rock and soil particles from one place to another
it forms mountains by pushing land up
exercises.exp: Erosion wears away the land — wind, water, and ice slowly carve valleys, wear down mountains, and shape coastlines over time.

exercises.question: Which force BUILDS UP land (deposition) while erosion WEARS it down?
choices: deposition builds up new landforms when eroded material is dropped; erosion removes material
deposition is faster than erosion always
erosion builds land and deposition removes it
exercises.exp: Erosion and deposition are partners — erosion removes material from one place; deposition drops it somewhere else, building new landforms!

exercises.question: The GRAND CANYON was formed by ___.
choices: the Colorado River eroding through rock layers over millions of years
exercises.exp: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon over about 5-6 million years — cutting through rock layers up to 1.6 km deep!

exercises.question: What is a FJORD?
choices: a flat treeless plain in cold regions
a long, narrow inlet of sea carved by a glacier, with steep cliff walls
exercises.exp: Fjords are spectacular — glaciers carved deep U-shaped valleys that filled with seawater. Norway's fjords are world-famous!

exercises.question: Sand dunes form in deserts because ___.
choices: wind picks up and drops sand grains, building up mound-shaped hills
rocks grind each other down into sand piles in one spot
exercises.exp: Wind carries sand grains and drops them when it slows — building dunes. Sand dunes can be enormous and even move over time!

exercises.question: What is CONTINENTAL DRIFT?
choices: the very slow movement of Earth's tectonic plates and continents over millions of years
exercises.exp: About 200 million years ago, all continents were joined as one supercontinent (Pangaea) — they slowly drifted to their current positions!

exercises.question: Why do we find FOSSILS of sea creatures on top of mountains?
choices: ancient seas covered that area; the rock (with fossils) was pushed up by tectonic forces over millions of years
mountains were always under the sea
exercises.exp: Tectonic forces can push ancient sea-floor rock upward to form mountains — carrying fossils of sea creatures to the summit! The Himalayas have sea fossils.

exercises.question: A WETLAND (marsh or swamp) is important because ___.
choices: it is useless land that should be drained
it filters water, provides habitat for wildlife, and reduces flooding by absorbing excess water
exercises.exp: Wetlands are incredibly valuable ecosystems — they clean water, support biodiversity, and act as natural flood barriers for communities!

exercises.question: What type of rock can contain FOSSILS?
choices: sedimentary rock — fossils are trapped in settling layers of sediment
exercises.exp: Fossils form in sedimentary rock — organisms are buried by sediment which hardens around them over millions of years. Igneous and metamorphic conditions destroy fossils.
